title: Architecture Standards: API, Coding, Infra, Model-Serving, Observability, Performance, and ADRs
author: Priya Nair
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates Redwood Inference's architecture and standards across API design, coding, infrastructure (IaC), model-serving, observability, performance, and the ADR (Architecture Decision Record) process. It establishes mandatory expectations for new services and guidelines for reviewing existing systems.

Scope: Applies to all internal and customer-facing services that are part of Redwood's runtime, control plane, SDKs, web consoles, and deployment artifacts. Exceptions require an ADR and security/infra owner sign-off.

Principles (high-level)
- Developer-first: APIs and infra should prioritize clarity, discoverability, and ergonomics for engineers and integrators.
- Production-first: Default choices must favor reliability, observability, and cost predictability.
- Reproducible and versioned: Everything produced (models, images, IaC) must be versioned and reproducible.
- Security and privacy by default: Secrets, keys, and customer data patterns must follow security-and-compliance guidance.

1) API Standards
- Surface: REST + JSON for public HTTP APIs; gRPC internal service-to-service where low-latency binary contracts are needed.
- Versioning: Use URI versioning (/v1/...) for public APIs; semantic versioning for SDKs and server components. Deprecation policy: 90 days notice for minor deprecations, 180 days for breaking changes.
- Naming: Use nouns for resources (POST /v1/inference/jobs), verbs for actions when needed (POST /v1/models/:id/rollout).
- Idempotency: Write operations must support idempotency keys (Idempotency-Key header).
- Errors: Return structured errors {"code":"string","message":"string","details":[]} with HTTP status between 4xx/5xx. Include consistent machine-readable codes (e.g., INVALID_REQUEST, QUOTA_EXCEEDED).
- Pagination: Use cursor-based pagination. Response envelope: {"items":[], "next_cursor": "..."}.
- Rate limiting: Per-API and per-key rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset).
- Auth: OAuth2 Bearer tokens for platform APIs; mTLS for internal gRPC channels.
- Telemetry: Attach request_id to every request, propagate in headers (X-Request-Id) and logs.
- Example payload (generation request):
{
  "model":"redwood/turbo-v1",
  "input":"Summarize the following...",
  "max_tokens":256,
  "stream":false
}

2) Coding Standards
- Languages: Primary back-end languages: Go (services), Python (ML infra, evaluations), and TypeScript (frontend & SDK).
- Style and formatting: Enforce gofmt/golangci-lint, black + isort + flake8 for Python, Prettier + ESLint for TypeScript.
- Testing: Unit tests >= 80% coverage for critical path; integration tests for APIs and model-serving; CI gates for PRs.
- Static checks: All PRs must pass linters, type checks (mypy/tsc), and license/third-party checks.
- Dependency updates: Use Dependabot or Renovate; major upgrades require ADR if they change runtime semantics.
- Secrets: Never check secrets into VCS. Use vault-backed secrets in CI and runtime.

3) Infrastructure Standards (IaC & Ops)
- IaC: Terraform for cloud infra modules; modules must be self-contained, documented, and live in the terraform/ monorepo.
- Environments: dev, staging, prod. Promote via automated pipelines with approval gates for prod.
- Resource tagging: All cloud resources must include tags: {"owner","service","env","cost-center"}.
- Networking: Default deny; only approved ports and CIDR blocks. Use VPC peering or private link for cross-account traffic.
- Secrets & KMS: Customer keys stored in customer-managed KMS where required; platform secrets in Vault with rotation policies.
- CI/CD: Immutable artifacts (container images, model bundles) with content-addressable tags and SBOMs.

4) Model-serving Standards
- Model packaging: Models must include manifest.json with model version, architecture, tokenizer spec, supported precisions, and recommended quantization profile.
- Quantization profiles: Maintain quantization-profiles directory (see prompt-sets-and-benchmarks) with recommended config for each model class.
- KV cache and state: KV caches for decoding must be versioned and validated in integration tests to avoid cache-compatibility regressions.
- Inference runtime compatibility: Runtime must declare supported op-kernels and minimal runtime version in serving manifest.
- Rollouts: Canary (5%/20%/100%) with automated quality gates (latency, token-level failure rate, quality regression metric).
- Fallbacks: Define compatible fallback models for each primary model to meet SLAs during degradation.

5) Observability Standards
- Metrics: Expose Prometheus metrics with the following conserved names: request_latency_seconds (histogram), tokens_generated_total (counter), model_inference_errors_total, batch_size. Metric labels: service, model, region, env.
- Tracing: Distributed tracing with W3C Trace-Context. Span conventions: top-level spans for request.accept, request.infer, request.stream. Sample at 10% by default; 100% sampling for errors above threshold.
- Logging: Structured JSON logs, 1 log entry per logical event. Include request_id, user/customer_id (when permitted), latency_ms, and model_version.
- Dashboards & Alerts: Per-service dashboards (latency, error rate, QPS, cost-per-token). Alert thresholds: p99 latency > SLO*1.5 for 10 minutes, error rate > 0.5% for 5 minutes.
- SLOs: Define SLOs in eng-sre/slo registry. Example: Public inference API: availability 99.9% monthly, p95 latency < 300ms for small models (<=512 tokens).

6) Performance Standards & Benchmarking
- Benchmark suite: Use eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite. Benchmarks must include cold start, steady-state throughput, latency percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99), and token-per-second metrics for representative sequences.
- Load testing: All tenant-impacting changes require pre-deploy load tests against staging with baseline comparison.
- Performance budgets: Services must publish cost and latency budgets. Example: small-model endpoint target cost <= $0.0005/token at median batch sizes and p95 latency < 250ms.
- Optimization guidelines: Prefer batching and KV caching before quantizing; quantization must be validated by regression-evals.

7) Architecture Decision Record (ADR) Process
- When: For any architecture decision that affects system topology, non-trivial cost/latency tradeoffs, compliance posture, or long-lived API/contract changes.
- Template (summary):
  - ADR-ID: ADR-YYYY-NN
  - Title: short title
  - Status: proposed | accepted | superseded | deprecated
  - Context: background and constraints
  - Decision: chosen alternative and rationale
  - Consequences: operational, cost, migration plan
  - Owners: team and primary approver
- Workflow: Author drafts ADR, solicits reviewers, publishes in confluence/architecture-and-standards, and raises PR for related RFC/infra changes. Acceptance requires two engineering reviewers and the relevant infra/security owner.
- Example ADR (summary): ADR-2025-07: "Switch internal RPC from REST to gRPC for low-latency model routing" — accepted; consequences included migration plan, compatibility shim, and rollout in three stages.

8) Review, Compliance and Ownership
- Periodic reviews: Every service must have an architecture review yearly to ensure compliance with these standards. Critical infra modules reviewed semi-annually.
- Owners: Each standard area has a documented owner (API standards: API Platform; Infra standards: Cloud Platform; Model-serving standards: Serving Runtime). See owners roster in the related_pages.

Appendix: Quick checklist for new service onboarding
1. Register service in service-catalog with owner and cost-center.
2. Create ADR if the design deviates from defaults.
3. Provide OpenAPI spec and generated client for public APIs.
4. Implement metrics/tracing/logs per conventions.
5. Add automated rollout plan and canary test.
6. Confirm IaC modules exist and pass security scan.
7. Add performance benchmark to perf-suite.

Contact & escalation
For questions and exceptions, contact the Architecture guild (arch-guild@redwood.internal) or open a ticket in #arch-standards. For urgent infra/security exceptions, page the on-call infra owner.
